newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: CRICKET-POLLOCK RESCUES S.AFRICA WITH TEST BEST 79.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-POLLOCK RESCUES S.AFRICA WITH TEST BEST 79.

text.p: Shaun Pollock struck his test best of 79 and shared a record stand with Brian McMillan to rescue South Africa in the third and final test against India at the Wanderers on Saturday.
Pollock and fellow all-rounder McMillan, who hit 47, put on 112 for the sixth wicket as their side made 321 all out at the close on the third day in reply to India's first innings of 410.
The last wicket fell in the final over of the day, Paul Adams becoming paceman Javagal Srinath's fifth victim to leave India leading by 89.
South Africa, with a 2-0 winning lead in the series, were hauled out of trouble as Pollock and McMillan took the score from 147 for five to 259 for six.
Their stand of 112 is a South African sixth wicket record against India. In the second test the same pair set a seventh wicet record with an unbroken stand of 101.
Pollock was eventually caught behind off Srinath with the second new ball, having hit 12 fours from 158 balls.
On 76, Pollock passed the highest test score of his father, selection convenor and former test fast bowler Peter.
South Africa, nought for no wicket overnight, batted freely all the way down the order, and only Pollock provided the long innings required for the situation.
Gary Kirsten (29), Daryll Cullinan (33) and Hansie Cronje (43) all savaged the Indian attack, but perished when well set.
Both Cullinan and Cronje fell to well directed short balls from Srinath, who was the pick of the bowlers and finished with five for 104.
Cronje, who has been battling for form, took on Srinath from the start and hit seven fours from 57 balls before top edging a hook to mid-wicket.
McMillan took his series aggregate to 294 and average to 147 before being trapped lbw by medium pacer Saurav Ganguly after hitting four boundaries from 83 balls.
